_comment: GENERATED by scripts/tt-gemm-ledger.py from scripts/tt-matmul-measure.sh runs. NEVER hand-edit: every row is re-parsed from its committed ttsim log excerpt by tt_sim_lock, and every comparison ratio is recomputed there. cycles = ttsim g_clock at simulator exit (the `[N] … seconds (… MHz)` heartbeat printed by ttsim_exit): whole program — device init + operand upload + program + read-back — on one global 1 GHz device timebase. No hardware, no watts. Rows whose knobs (math fidelity / fp32 accumulate / packer L1-accumulate) differ are NEVER a head-to-head: they live in unmatched_comparisons and may be quoted only with both fidelity labels.
cycle_definition: last `[N] … seconds (… MHz|KHz)` heartbeat line of the ttsim run (ttsim src/sim.cpp ttsim_exit)

stacks.logos_emitted: the LOGOS compiler's own emitted tt-metal program; `generated` says which parts
stacks.tt_metal_example: a stock tt-metal programming example under tt_metal/programming_examples/matmul/, unmodified
stacks.ttnn_production: the vendor's production op ttnn.matmul called from Python under ttsim

clock_validity.evidence: K doubled at fixed M,N moves no kernel-reachable counter: 640x640x320/640/1280 -> 5678/5562/5562; the 1024 family -> 6205 at K=512,1024,2048; compute TRISC spans 660->658, 690->682, 919->921, while host wall-clock rises almost linearly
clock_validity.consequence: ratios computed from `cycles` are NOT speed claims; a defensible speed number needs silicon, where the device wall-clock register is real
clock_validity.what_survives: correctness (PCC), program identity, and orderings that do not assert time

work_meter.instrument: ttsim (Apache-2.0) + a counters-only patch: TTSIM_OP_STATS / TTSIM_DONE / TTSIM_STALLS
work_meter.timing_identity_evidence: matmul_single_core reports 330268 cycles under the stock release .so and under the instrumented build — the patch adds counters and moves no clock
work_meter.evidence: 512x512xK, K swept 512->4096 (8x): tensix_inst 140048->1136400 (8.11x), matmul_retired 262144->2097152 (8.000x, exact), noc_txns 4480->33152 (7.40x), noc_bytes 8914816->67635072 (7.59x) — while g_clock moved 5180->5184 and device_cycles 372->373

fields.matmul_issued: MVMUL issues INCLUDING the retry-spin an operand-starved core performs; a stall meter, not a work meter — `matmul_retired` is the work
fields.matmul_retired: MVMULs that actually retired. A CONSERVATION LAW: two programs computing the same GEMM retire the same count, whoever emitted them, so every other counter beside it is a like-for-like efficiency comparison and not a difference in what was computed
fields.tensix_inst: Tensix instructions issued across the device
fields.stall_srca: cycles a math op waited on source register A

work_meter.consequence: these are functions of the program, so these — never `cycles` — are what the cost model is fitted to and what a compiler comparison may be made on

corrections.what: noc_bytes counted an atomic's instruction word and an inline write's byte-enable mask as if they were transfer lengths
corrections.detail: ttsim's `noc_at_len_be` register is a LENGTH only on reads, writes and multicasts. On a semaphore atomic it carries NOC_AT_WRAP(31)|NOC_AT_INS_INCR_GET = 0x107C..0x107F, which sits inside NOC_MAX_PACKET_SIZE and was being added as 4,222 bytes for a transfer that moves FOUR. The meter charged every program for its handshakes at a thousand times their weight, and it is not a neutral error: it flatters whichever stack synchronizes less.
corrections.found_by: predicting the 512x512x512 multicast plan's NOC bytes from its choreography and missing by exactly one atomic per receiver per K block
corrections.effect: 512^3 multicast-split read 3,095,224 bytes before the fix and 2,622,240 after, against 2,621,440 predicted from the program — a 0.03% agreement where there had been 18%. Every row was re-measured afterwards.
